uncited: Hatching and Stroke-based Rendering (Hatching) is a family of non-photorealistic volume rendering techniques that simulate hand-drawn line art, such as hatching, stippling, or paint strokes, to convey shape, spatial relationships, and aesthetic qualities of 3D volumetric data.
It solves the problem of abstracting continuous volumetric features into discrete, interpretable graphical elements that mimic traditional artistic media.
Compute associated orientations θ0, θ1, θ2 to position control points A, B, C, D.
Vary w to w1, w2 such that 0 <= w1, w2 < w/8.
Draw q2 opposite q1 with length l, width w2, color C2.
The origins of stroke-based volume rendering lie in the broader field of Non-Photorealistic Rendering (NPR) applied to scientific visualization.
Early work focused on surface-based hatching and contouring.
The application of these techniques to volumetric data required new approaches to handle the continuous nature of volumes.
